headline: Turner's walk-off single beats Nationals in the 9th
recap: In the bottom of the ninth, Brandon Marsh singled and advanced to second on a throwing error by Nationals right fielder Alex Call. Pinch-hitter Cal Stevenson bunted his way aboard to send Marsh to third, and Washington intentionally walked Kyle Schwarber to load the bases before Trea Turner lined a single to left, scoring Marsh and giving the Phillies a 3-2 walk-off win over the Nationals at Citizens Bank Park. Washington had tied the game at 2-2 an inning earlier when closer Carlos Estévez allowed three hits and two runs in the top of the ninth, blowing his fourth save of the season.

Phillies starter Aaron Nola worked 6.2 innings and allowed seven hits but no runs, walking two and striking out four. Nationals starter Patrick Corbin lasted 4.1 innings and was charged with both of Philadelphia's runs on seven hits, two walks and two strikeouts.

Turner finished 4-for-5 with a double in addition to the winning hit. Philadelphia's first two runs came in the third inning, when Nick Castellanos' two-out single scored Turner and J.T. Realmuto followed with a single that brought home Castellanos. Matt Strahm and Jeff Hoffman combined for 1.1 scoreless relief innings before Estévez's shaky ninth.
